version.changelog: Initial release - auto-fetch transcripts, generate structured summaries, and send to Telegram

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: youtube-summarizer
Version: 1.0.0

The skill is classified as suspicious due to its reliance on an external GitHub repository (`https://github.com/kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript`) for its core functionality. Both `SKILL.md` and `package.json` instruct the agent to `git clone` this repository into `/root/clawd/mcp-server-youtube-transcript`, followed by `npm install` and `npm run build`, and then execute Node.js code from it. This introduces a significant supply chain risk, as the integrity of the external repository cannot be guaranteed, and its code is executed with the agent's permissions. Additionally, the skill writes full transcripts to `/root/clawd/transcripts/`, which involves privileged directory access. While the stated purpose of YouTube summarization appears benign, the method of fetching and executing code from an external, potentially unvetted source, combined with system-level file operations, raises security concerns.

llm.summary: The skill does what it claims, but its install and transcript-fetch workflow give too much unsafe execution and data-sharing authority without enough controls.

dimensions.detail: The documented paths under /root/clawd and command execution are broader than needed for routine summarization, especially when combined with persistent transcript files and Telegram delivery.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation clones a third-party GitHub repository from its mutable default branch and runs npm install plus npm run build without a pinned commit, checksum, lockfile requirement, or sandboxing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions accept 11-character direct video IDs and tell the agent to substitute them into a double-quoted shell command, with no allowlist validation; they also use a fixed shared /tmp output path.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill intentionally stores full transcripts under /root/clawd/transcripts and may send them to Telegram; this is disclosed, but there is no consent gate, retention limit, cleanup path, or destination confirmation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Fetching YouTube transcripts, summarizing them, saving files, and sending Telegram attachments matches the stated purpose, but the workflow relies on shell execution with user-derived video IDs and automatic full-transcript handling.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable running unpinned third-party Node code and storing full transcripts locally. Treat YouTube IDs or URLs as untrusted input, avoid private or sensitive videos, confirm Telegram destinations before sending files, and prefer a version that pins dependencies, validates video IDs with a strict allowlist, uses unique temporary files, and offers transcript retention controls.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Artifact inspection supports the concern: the skill tells the agent to insert a user-derived VIDEO_ID into an inline shell command and write to a predictable /tmp file, creating avoidable command-injection and file-collision risk.
[T08] unexpected: Artifact inspection supports the concern: a transcript dependency is purpose-aligned, but cloning and building unpinned external code at install time is not adequately constrained.
[SQP-2] expected: Saving and Telegram delivery are part of the advertised behavior, so this is not hidden exfiltration; however, the artifacts lack clear consent, retention, and third-party-sharing controls.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The transcript retrieval capability is expected, but the specific mechanism uses broad shell and Node execution where a narrower, preinstalled, validated tool would fit the purpose better.
[SQP-3] expected: Language fallback is disclosed and low impact compared with the execution and persistence issues; users should still know when fallback changes the requested language.
